title: How are FD interest rates changing from October 1? There's good news for bulk depositors
description: The Reserve Bank of India is introducing new regulations from October 1, 2026, to bring transparency to how commercial banks display and decide interest rates on deposits, especially for bulk deposits of ₹3 crore and above. Prompted by an incident involving HDFC Bank, the RBI's 'Amendment Directions' will require banks to publish their bulk deposit rates daily on their official websites by 10:00 am. While generally ensuring uniformity, banks will have the flexibility to offer differential rates on bulk deposits based on assessed asset risk, using measures like the LCR run-off rate. These new rules apply to new bulk and term deposits, including NRI rupee deposits, but will not alter existing retail fixed deposit plans or cause daily fluctuations for regular customers.

title: How are FD interest rates changing from October 1? There's good news for bulk depositors
description: The Reserve Bank of India is introducing new regulations from October 1, 2026, to bring transparency to how commercial banks display and decide interest rates on deposits, especially for bulk deposits of ₹3 crore and above. Prompted by an incident involving HDFC Bank, the RBI's 'Amendment Directions' will require banks to publish their bulk deposit rates daily on their official websites by 10:00 am. While generally ensuring uniformity, banks will have the flexibility to offer differential rates on bulk deposits based on assessed asset risk, using measures like the LCR run-off rate. These new rules apply to new bulk and term deposits, including NRI rupee deposits, but will not alter existing retail fixed deposit plans or cause daily fluctuations for regular customers.
